title: Notch, Peak or Shawl: Choosing a Lapel Style
excerpt: The lapel shape changes the whole character of a jacket more than almost any other detail. Here's how to choose.
author: Lipek Fashion Team
body: Notch lapels are the most versatile and the safest default for business suits — a clean, moderate angle that works for almost any body type and occasion.
Peak lapels point upward and outward, adding visual width to the chest and shoulder. They read as more formal and more assertive, which is why they're common on double-breasted jackets and tuxedos.
Shawl lapels curve without a break at all, giving a smooth, rounded line. Traditionally reserved for formal evening wear like dinner jackets, though we've cut them for modern occasion pieces too.
As a rule of thumb: notch for everyday and business, peak for a stronger formal statement, shawl for black-tie and evening events.
